match.reason: No bank point teaches the rule that joined faces are left out of a composite solid's surface area: mat-surface-area and mat-surface-area-volume cover only single solids, and mat-shapes-objects covers the joining idea only for 2D outlines, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Surface area of composite solids
card: Surface area is the total area of the faces on the outside of a solid.
When two parts are joined, the faces that touch are hidden inside. Leave them out.
Method: find the surface area of each part, then subtract the area of every hidden face. If a small part sits on a larger face, that part of the large face is hidden too.
Example: two cubes of side 1 cm are stacked. Each has area 6 cm², so 12 − 2 = 10 cm², as two 1 cm² faces are hidden.
draft.remember: Add the outside faces only. Every join hides a face on each part.

a.q: Two cubes of side 2 cm are stacked to make a 2 cm by 2 cm by 4 cm prism. What is the surface area?
a.why: Each cube has surface area 6 × 4 = 24 cm², so 48 cm² together. The join hides one 4 cm² face on each cube, which is 8 cm². So 48 − 8 = 40 cm². Subtracting only one hidden face gives 44 cm², which is wrong.
a.clue: Each cube loses a face where they touch.

b.q: A cube of side 4 cm has a cube of side 2 cm sitting on top of it. What is the total surface area?
b.why: The cubes have 96 + 24 = 120 cm² separately. The join hides 4 cm² on the small cube's base and 4 cm² on the large cube's top, so 120 − 8 = 112 cm². Subtracting only one hidden face gives 116 cm².
b.clue: The large cube's top is covered where the small cube sits.

problems.detail: "Every join hides a face on each part" clashes with the card, which says that when a small part sits on a larger face, only part of the large face is hidden. In question b the large cube loses only 4 cm² of its 16 cm² top, not a whole face.

check.summary: Both answers check out: 40 cm² for a and 112 cm² for b, and the explanations agree. The remember line says each join hides a whole face on each part, which contradicts the card's point that only part of a larger face is hidden.

proposal.title: Surface area of composite solids
card: Surface area is the total area of the faces on the outside of a solid.
When two parts are joined, the areas that touch are hidden inside. Leave them out of the total.
Method: add the surface areas of the parts, then subtract the touching area twice, once for each part. If a small part sits on a larger face, only the covered part of that face is hidden.
Example: two cubes of side 1 cm are stacked. Each has area 6 cm², so 12 − 2 = 10 cm², as a 1 cm² face is hidden on each cube.
proposal.remember: Count the outside only. Subtract the touching area once for each part that touches.

a.q: Two cubes of side 2 cm are stacked to make a 2 cm by 2 cm by 4 cm prism. What is the surface area?
a.why: Each cube has surface area 6 × 4 = 24 cm², so 48 cm² together. The join hides one 4 cm² face on each cube, which is 8 cm², so 48 − 8 = 40 cm². Subtracting the hidden area only once gives 44 cm², which is wrong.
a.clue: Each cube loses a face where they touch.

b.q: A cube of side 4 cm has a cube of side 2 cm sitting on top of it. What is the total surface area?
b.why: The cubes have 96 + 24 = 120 cm² separately. The join hides the small cube's 4 cm² base and the 4 cm² of the large cube's top that it covers, so 120 − 8 = 112 cm². Subtracting the touching area only once gives 116 cm².
b.clue: Only the covered part of the large cube's top is hidden.
